Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: speechToTextMarkup
candidates.comment: An identification of the markup format used for pronounceable text, such as SSML or IPA. Also called "pronunciation markup", "text-to-speech format", "phonetic notation". Examples: "The pronounceable text uses speechToTextMarkup SSML", "The dictionary entry has speechToTextMarkup IPA", "This text's speechToTextMarkup specifies pronunciation details."

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: tickerSymbol
candidates.comment: A textual identifier representing the exchange-traded instrument associated with a corporation, typically an exchange and instrument name. Also called "stock symbol", "stock ticker", "exchange symbol", "trading symbol". Examples: "Apple Inc. has tickerSymbol NASDAQ AAPL", "The corporation's tickerSymbol is NYSE GOOG", "This company is identified by its tickerSymbol."

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: logo
candidates.comment: A logo relation between a brand, certification, organization, place, product, or service and its associated image or URL. Also called: brand logo, official emblem, corporate identity. Examples: "Apple Inc. logo Apple Logo Image", "Nike Product logo Nike Swoosh", "Olympic Games logo Olympic Rings".

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: identifyingExam
candidates.comment: An identifying exam relation between a medical sign and a physical examination that can detect it. Also called diagnostic exam, detection exam, exam for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying exam of a neurological check.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying exam.", "This sign requires an identifying exam."

candidates.label: recordLabel
candidates.comment: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

chosen_property.label: releaseNotes
chosen_property.justification: The 'releaseNotes' property from schema.org matches the observed signature and definition.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: releaseNotes
candidates.comment: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: albumRelease
candidates.comment: An album release relation between a music album and a specific release instance of that album. Also called album edition, release version, publication. Examples: "A music album's album release is its 'Deluxe Edition'.", "The album's album release is its 'Vinyl Remaster'."

candidates.label: musicReleaseFormat
candidates.comment: The format of a music release, indicating the type of recording media. Also called release format, media type, recording format. Examples: "Album X musicReleaseFormat 'CDFormat'", "Single Y musicReleaseFormat 'DigitalAudioTapeFormat'", "LP Z musicReleaseFormat 'VinylFormat'".

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

chosen_property.label: conductsAnalysis
chosen_property.definition: To examine or evaluate something, often using specialized techniques or methods, in order to understand or interpret its characteristics or implications.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the observed signature and definition.

candidates.label: chemicalComposition
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a chemical substance, detailing its identity and relative ratio of chemical elements. Also called "molecular formula", "chemical makeup", "compositional analysis". Examples: "Water chemical substance chemicalComposition 'H2O'", "Salt chemical substance chemicalComposition 'NaCl'".

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: interactionStatistic
candidates.comment: An interaction metric relation between a creative work, organization, or person, and a counter that quantifies user interactions with it. Also called engagement metrics, user activity, interaction data, usage statistics. Examples: A blog post has an interactionStatistic of a 'LikeAction' counter. An organization has an interactionStatistic of a 'CommentAction' counter. A person has an interactionStatistic of a 'ShareAction' counter.

candidates.label: reviews
candidates.comment: A collection of critical assessments or evaluations pertaining to an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item reviews, evaluations, critiques, assessments. Examples: `Product: Laptop` reviews `[Review 1, Review 2, ...]`, `Movie: Dune` reviews `[Critic Review, User Review]`, `Restaurant: Pizzeria` reviews `[Google Reviews, Yelp Reviews]`. Distinct from `review`, which typically refers to a single review.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

chosen_property.label: comment
chosen_property.justification: The 'comment' property from schema.org matches the observed signature and definition.

chosen_property.label: comment
chosen_property.justification: The 'comment' property from schema.org matches the observed signature and definition.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: comment
candidates.comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: commentText
candidates.comment: A textual content relation for user comments, providing the actual text of the comment. Also called "comment content", "message text", "user feedback text". Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.

candidates.label: replyToUrl
candidates.comment: A reply URL relation between user comments and the web address where a response can be submitted. Also called comment reply link, response URL. Examples: "A user comment has a reply to URL 'http://example.com/comment/123/reply'.", "A forum post has a reply to URL 'http://forum.com/thread/456#reply'.", "A blog comment has a reply to URL 'http://blog.com/post/789/comment'."

candidates.label: discussionUrl
candidates.comment: A discussion URL relation between a creative work and the URL of the page where its comments are located. Also called "comments page link", "forum link", "feedback URL". Examples: "Movie 'Inception' discussionUrl 'example.com/inception/comments'", "Article 'Quantum Physics' discussionUrl 'forum.example.org/quantum'", "Book '1984' discussionUrl 'goodreads.com/1984/discussion'". Distinct from discusses, which is the creative work that a user comment is about.

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".
